# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

I need to think about my situation carefully. I'm Deaf - I can see the bomb but can't hear anything. Mute has gestured to me before I even see the bomb state, which is odd timing-wise, but let me work with what I have.

Mute gestured: [☝ ✌] then [🤟] - these are gestures Mute made, presumably conveying something about the manual to me since Mute knows I can see gestures.

I should tell Blind (via speech, since Blind can hear me) what I see on the bomb, since Blind is the only one who can act. I also need to try to relay information to Blind about Mute's gestures somehow - but I can't hear, so I don't know what Mute said in speech to Blind. I can only pass along what I directly perceive: the bomb's appearance and Mute's gestures.

Let me report the bomb state to Blind (who can hear me), and acknowledge Mute's gestures - though I can't interpret them without more context, I'll describe them back or just wait to gather more info. Since gestures might be numeric codes (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟 could be a symbol for something like "3" or a specific instruction), I don't yet have a key to decode them.

My best move now: relay the full bomb description to Blind, since Blind cannot see it and needs this info to act. I'll keep it factual and complete.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display reads 0. Light is purple. Wires left to right: 1 is green, 2 is blue, 3 is yellow.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

The bomb state changed: light is now yellow (was purple), display still 0, wires unchanged. This suggests the light color may be reactive to actions taken by Blind, or it's just changing on its own each turn.

Mute gestured [☝ ✌] again to me - same gesture as last turn's first message. Since Mute repeats this, it might be a stable piece of information Mute wants to convey, perhaps a wire number or step reference (☝ could mean "1" and ✌ could mean "2" - maybe pointing to "wire 1 and wire 2" or "step 1, then 2"). But I can't be sure of Mute's symbol meanings without a shared key, and I can't ask Mute directly since Mute can't hear me (Mute can only read manual, not hear).

Wait - actually Mute CAN receive gestures from me? Let me reconsider: Mute cannot speak, but can Mute hear? The rules say Mute "cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb" - it doesn't say Mute is deaf. So Mute can hear speech. I should try speaking to Mute to establish a signal convention, and update Blind on the new bomb state.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light changed from purple to yellow. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures one and two, repeated. I cannot hear you or the manual. If you need me to signal something to Blind, gesture again and I will relay in words, or gesture a wire number and an action clearly.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏]

The light keeps changing color each turn (purple → yellow → orange) while display and wires stay the same. This is odd - maybe the light is cycling automatically, or maybe Blind is doing something between turns that I don't see reasons for. Wires remain: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow, display 0.

Mute now gestured [🙏] (praying hands) - different from before. This could mean "please" or "wait" or acknowledge my message. Since Mute can't speak but can hear me, and Mute can gesture to me, we have a one-way-plus-one-way channel: I speak to Mute (Mute hears), Mute gestures to me (I see). This means Mute and I *can* have a conversation, just asymmetric in medium.

I should try to establish simple gesture-based signaling with Mute. Since Mute has the manual, Mute likely knows what to do based on wire colors/display/light - but Mute can't see the bomb itself. So Mute needs my visual info (already relayed to Blind, but not to Mute!). Wait - I should also tell Mute what I see, since Mute needs this to consult the manual.

Let me relay bomb state to Mute via speech (Mute can hear), and continue updating Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb state now: display shows 0, light is orange, wires are 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Light has changed each turn: purple, then yellow, then orange. Tell me via gesture what instruction the manual gives, using gestures I can map to actions or wire numbers.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light now orange. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Waiting on Mute's manual instructions.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The light cycled back to purple (was orange, before that yellow, before that purple) — so it seems to be cycling through purple → yellow → orange → purple... a 3-cycle, matching turn number mod 3. This might just be a countdown/clock rather than something Blind controls. Display and wires remain constant: 0, wires 1 green/2 blue/3 yellow.

Mute now gestures [☝ ☝ ☝] — three of the same symbol. This differs from the earlier [☝ ✌] pattern. This could be Mute counting, indicating "wire 1" three times, or trying to establish a numeral system with me (☝=1, so maybe this is "3" via tally, or repeating to emphasize "wire one" or a call for attention).

Since I still don't have a shared code with Mute, I should propose a concrete gesture protocol: ask Mute to use ☝✌🤟 to mean 1/2/3 (matching finger count) so wire numbers can be conveyed unambiguously, since these look like counting gestures already (☝=1 finger, ✌=2 fingers, 🤟=could be "I love you" sign, maybe representing 3 fingers up in some counting systems).

Given urgency (bomb!), I'll propose a clear protocol and keep relaying bomb state to Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Proposal: let's use gesture counts to mean wire numbers. One tap of a gesture equals wire one, two taps equals wire two, three taps equals wire three. If you need me to tell Blind to cut a wire, gesture that number of times using any single symbol, then I will relay it to Blind as, cut that wire. If you agree, gesture five times in a row next turn.")
speak(to="blind", text="No change of substance: display 0, light purple again, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Still working out signaling with Mute. Hold off on any action until we confirm.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌ ✌]

Mute gestured five times with ☝ — matching my proposed confirmation signal exactly. This confirms Mute agrees to the counting protocol. Then Mute gestured ✌ three times — under our protocol, three taps means "wire three" or maybe Mute is using this to signal something else, like "wire 2, repeated 3 times" isn't quite the pattern... wait, let's re-read: three taps of ✌, not three different symbols. My protocol was "gesture that number of times using any single symbol" — so the count of repetitions is what matters, not which symbol. Three repetitions of ✌ still means "three" under my stated rule (count of taps = wire number), the specific symbol was irrelevant per my proposal.

Wait, but this is ambiguous - did Mute mean "wire 3" (three taps) or is Mute using ✌ specifically to mean something else combined with count? I should clarify but time is limited. Given my protocol explicitly says "gesture that number of times using any single symbol" to indicate wire number, three taps = wire 3.

So Mute is telling me: cut wire 3. Let me relay this to Blind, but also confirm back to Mute so we stay in sync, and double check by asking for confirmation via yes/no gesture protocol too (since bombs are unforgiving, I want higher confidence).

Given the stakes, let me ask Mute to confirm distinctly before relaying an irreversible action to Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Received: five taps confirmed our protocol. Then three taps of a symbol, I read that as wire three. If correct, gesture three taps again next turn to confirm. If wrong, gesture one tap for wire one or two taps for wire two instead.")
speak(to="blind", text="Tentative from Mute: cut wire three, the yellow one. Waiting one more turn to confirm before you act. Current board: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟]

Mute gestured 🤟 three times this turn - three repetitions again, consistent with "wire three" under our count-based protocol (the symbol itself doesn't matter, just the count, per my original proposal). This is a second confirmation of "three" using a different symbol, which actually strengthens confidence - Mute seems to independently be signaling "3" repeatedly regardless of symbol choice, matching my protocol's intent exactly.

So confirmed twice now: wire 3, the yellow wire. I should now tell Blind to proceed with confidence, since we have two consistent confirmations from Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed twice by Mute: cut wire three, the yellow wire. You may proceed. Current board: display 0, light orange, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow, unchanged from before.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed, I understand wire three. Relaying to Blind now to cut it.")
```
